chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade placing the embalming material (camphor) upon the coffin.

key_terms.النَّعْشِ: The coffin or bier used to carry the deceased
key_terms.الْحَنُوطُ: Embalming material, specifically camphor or musk used for preservation and fragrance

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet forbid regarding the placement of embalming material on the coffin?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s prohibition against applying 'hanut' (a mixture of musk, camphor, and other scents) directly onto the coffin or shroud, distinguishing it from the ritual washing (ghusl) where such scents are recommended. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling emphasizes simplicity in burial and prevents the waste of precious materials, reflecting the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams who preferred modesty in funeral preparations over ostentatious display.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> forbade from places the embalming material (camphor) upon the coffin’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said
the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Holy prophet prohibited placing of hunut on a coffin.’”
